page.query: Community as a Service vs. an in-house community team
page.title: Community as a Service vs In-House Team
page.description: Compare Community as a Service and an in-house community team on cost, control, speed and risk. Get a decision checklist, staffing model table and FAQ.
page.h1: Community as a Service vs an in-house community team
page.definition: Community as a Service is an outsourced model where an external partner handles strategy, moderation, programming, onboarding and reporting on platforms such as Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups. An in-house community team is a dedicated internal group that owns the same workstreams with full brand authority and product integration.
page.quick_answer: Choose Community as a Service when you need coverage across time zones, variable member volume or specialised moderation without hiring. Build in-house when community is a core product differentiator, requires deep product feedback loops or demands brand voice control at every touchpoint.

sections.h2: What does each model actually cover day to day?

blocks.p: Community as a Service typically delivers moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting under a scoped agreement. An in-house team owns those same workstreams plus strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions.

ul: Moderation and safety enforcement across time zones
Member support tickets and escalation paths
New member onboarding flows and welcome sequences
Monthly health reports: activation, retention, sentiment

sections.h2: How do staffing and cost structures compare?

blocks.p: In-house means fixed headcount: community manager, moderator, analyst, strategist, plus benefits and tools. Community as a Service converts those roles into a variable fee tied to coverage hours, member volume and moderation risk.

sections.h2: When does each model make strategic sense?

blocks.p: The decision turns on whether community is a core product loop or a marketing channel, how fast you need coverage, and whether you can absorb hiring risk.

ol: Map community goals to product roadmap: if community drives feature feedback, keep strategy in-house
Audit current coverage gaps: nights, weekends, language support
Estimate member volume trajectory for the next twelve months
Score moderation risk: regulated topics, high conflict, user-generated content
Run a pilot: three months with a scoped Community as a Service partner, measure activation and sentiment
Revisit build versus buy at the pilot review gate

sections.h2: What governance and tools keep quality high?

blocks.p: Both models need a shared operating system: style guide, escalation matrix, content calendar, reporting cadence and approval gates. West Peek Productions sets up human-in-the-loop workflows so AI drafts never publish without a named approver.

ul: Style guide covering tone, terminology, crisis scripts
Escalation matrix with response time targets
Shared calendar in Asana, Monday.com or Airtable
Briefs in Google Docs or Notion with approval fields
Monthly health dashboard in GA4 or HubSpot
Quarterly business review with product and marketing leads

sections.h2: How do you transition without losing momentum?

blocks.p: Transition risk is highest during hand-off of member relationships, historical context and tribal knowledge. Plan a two-week overlap, document every workflow and assign a single internal owner for the partner relationship.

ul: Export member notes, tags and segmentation from current tools
Run joint moderation shifts for ten business days
Transfer ownership of programming calendar and recurring events
Align reporting definitions: active member, churn, sentiment score
Schedule weekly sync with partner account lead and internal sponsor

faq.q: What platforms does Community as a Service typically support?
faq.a: Common platforms include Discord, Slack, Circle, Discourse, Khoros, Higher Logic and LinkedIn groups. A partner should demonstrate live moderation experience on at least two of these before you sign.

faq.q: How is Community as a Service priced?
faq.a: West Peek Productions quotes by scope covering coverage hours, member volume, moderation risk and programming complexity. There is no fixed price list; send the scope for a quote.

faq.q: Can I keep strategy in-house while outsourcing operations?
faq.a: Yes. Keep in-house: strategy, brand voice approval and product decisions. Outsource: moderation, member support, programming, onboarding and reporting. This split is the most common hybrid model.

faq.q: What is the typical ramp period for a new Community as a Service engagement?
faq.a: Expect days to weeks after scope sign-off for the partner to staff coverage, ingest your style guide and begin moderation. A two-week joint shift period reduces risk.

faq.q: How do I measure whether the model is working?
faq.a: Track activation rate, retention at thirty and ninety days, sentiment trend, moderation response time and escalation volume. Review monthly with product and marketing leads; adjust scope quarterly.
